note: Format of IELTS Academic (the slot formerly used for TestDaF). Structure only: parts, question counts, timings, word counts and answer forms. As of 2026-10-30, from the public description of the test on ielts.org; the page was not re-fetched when this file was written, so entries marked "verify": true (finer details such as the timing of single speaking parts, the extra transfer time on paper, and the kinds of recordings and texts) should be checked once by hand against ielts.org before publication. The tasks, texts, charts and recordings of the real test are protected by copyright and are NOT in this file. IELTS can be taken on paper or on a computer; the content is the same, and Speaking is always a face-to-face interview with an examiner (in person or by video call).
grading: Each skill (Listening, Reading, Writing, Speaking) gets a band score from 0 to 9, in half bands where reported. The overall band is the average of the four scores, rounded to the nearest half band. There is no pass mark: each university, employer or immigration body sets the bands it asks for.
pilotNote: This practice site's own set (testdaf/uebungssatz-1.json) has Reading (30 questions) and Writing Task 1 only. Listening and Speaking are not part of it.

rows.type: Conversation between two people in an everyday social setting
Monologue in an everyday social setting
Conversation of up to four people in an educational or training setting

sections.note: Each recording is played once. Question types include multiple choice, matching, form or note completion, and short answers.

sections.label: Reading

rows.text: long text on an academic subject
long text on an academic subject
long text on an academic subject

sections.note: 40 questions in total over three passages. Question types include multiple choice, matching headings or information, True / False / Not given and Yes / No / Not given, and sentence or summary completion.

rows.type: Task 1: describe a chart, graph, table or diagram
Task 2: essay in response to a point of view, argument or problem

sections.note: Task 2 counts for more than Task 1 in the Writing band.

Two-way discussion of more abstract questions linked to the topic

sections.note: Face to face with an examiner; the interview is recorded.
